title: GPU stack bundle registry + rolling upgrade harness for immutable driver/CUDA contracts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Upgrading container images, CUDA toolkits, and GPU drivers across Dedicated and Private deployments is fragile. Failures often come from mismatched driver ABI/host kernel or from images whose SBOMs are stale relative to the runtime driver. We need a single source of truth that ties an immutable container image digest to an SBOM and a pinned GPU stack (CUDA version + driver ABI hash + kernel compatibility hints), plus tooling to run safe rolling upgrades with canary gating and automated rollback.

Goal: Build a Bundle Registry and Rolling Upgrade Harness that: 1) Stores immutable bundles (image digest, SPDX SBOM blob, driver pin metadata, compatibility contract), 2) Exposes an API for the scheduler/orchestrator to resolve a deployable bundle for a given LTS channel and workload profile, 3) Provides a controller that can execute staged rollouts with programmable gates (perf regressions, OOMs, driver faults) and automatic rollback, 4) Integrates with CI to publish bundles during image promotion and with Console to surface bundle-level telemetry and blame.

Non-goals: Replacing container registries; building a new package manager for drivers. We will interoperate with existing registries and driver repositories via metadata indexing.
acceptance_criteria: Registry stores bundle records that include: image_digest, sbom_url (SPDX JSON), cuda_major_minor, driver_abi_hash, host_kernel_hints, compatibility_tags
API can return the latest LTS bundle for a channel (e.g., runtime-lts-1.2) and for an explicit workload fingerprint
Upgrade harness can perform a canary roll across Dedicated pool and detect regressions via Console metrics (latency, token cost, driver crash_count) and automatically rollback on threshold breaches
CI publishes a bundle record on image promotion and attaches SBOM artifact; Console shows bundle traceability to PR and build id
Rollout audit log includes bundle id, step timestamps, observed metric deltas, and the responsible operator/automation id
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect kernel compatibility hints lead to node-level failures. Mitigation: conservative default require explicit kernel test pass before marking compatibility_tags=true for a kernel range.
Risk: SBOM drift if images are rebased without republishing. Mitigation: CI gate prevents image publish unless SBOM artifact exists and checksum matches image-label-spdx-reference.
Risk: Rollout harness acting on stale metrics. Mitigation: use event-windowed evaluation (5m/15m) and require confirmation step for high-impact upgrades (P0 safety threshold).
design_decisions: Use immutable bundle id: sha256(image_digest)+short driver_abi hash as canonical key
Store SBOM as an OCI artifact (SPDX JSON) referenced by digest; mirror to internal blobstore for retention guarantees
Compatibility contract is a small YAML blob with machine-consumable fields: cuda_version, driver_abi_hash, kernel_ranges, validated_tests (list of test ids)
Expose read-only bundle API to Customer-facing Console; control-plane components call the full registry API
Prefer non-blocking rollouts by default with autoscale-aware canaries; make synchronous (blocking) rollouts an explicit operator action
implementation_plan: MVP (2 sprints): implement bundle metadata schema + indexer in registry service, CI publisher hook, store SBOM mirrors, and a read API for bundles
Phase 2 (3-4 sprints): rollout harness controller with canary/linear strategies; integrate with Console metrics and tracing; add audit logs
Phase 3: hardening: kernel test matrix automation, signed bundle attestations, RBAC for bundle mutators, and retention/GC policies
testing_plan: Synthetic upgrade tests in staging: perform rolling upgrades across a 10-node dedicated pool with fault injection (OOM, driver-kernel panic) and assert rollback triggers
Compatibility fuzz: run small matrix of CUDA minor versions and driver ABI variants against representative model containers and record pass/fail
Canary metrics: validate harness triggers on latency delta > 10% or driver crash_count increase > 1 per minute during canary window
CI gating: require successful bundle record publish and SBOM checksum verification before promoting to LTS channel
rollout_plan: Start with non-customer-facing internal Dedicated pools. Enable canary size 3% of capacity, evaluation window 10 minutes, escalation to 20% if metrics stable. After 72h of stability promote to full pool rollout. For Private/VPC customers, expose 'opt-in auto-upgrade' flag; default is manual for first two LTS releases.
notes: Design review scheduled with Infra on 2025-02-20 (agenda: storage retention, signed attestations, KMS integration).
PM feedback: make the bundle contract minimal to avoid cross-team churn; prefer schema v1 with explicit opt-in for additional fields.
Follow-up: coordinate with Solutions Eng to draft customer migration notes for Private deployments that opt into auto-upgrades.
